tests: the tagging command fails closed on a pre-existing tag, and does not move, delete or reuse it

dangerousStates.find:
echo "tag: ${tag} already exists in this checkout at $(git rev-parse "refs/tags/${tag}")." >&2
            echo "tag: refusing, and NOT moving, deleting or reusing it. Recover by hand for ${tag} at ${SHA}." >&2
            exit 1

probe=0
          git ls-remote --exit-code --tags origin "refs/tags/${tag}" >/dev/null || probe=$?
          if [ "$probe" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "tag: ${tag} already exists on the remote." >&2
            echo "tag: refusing, and NOT moving, deleting or reusing it. Recover by hand for ${tag} at ${SHA}." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if [ "$probe" -ne 2 ]; then
            echo "tag: could not read the remote's tags; git ls-remote exited ${probe}." >&2
            echo "tag: refusing rather than assuming ${tag} is absent. Recover by hand for ${tag} at ${SHA}." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          # ANNOTATED, never lightweight: an annotated tag carries its own
          # object with an author and a date, which is what makes it a record
          # rather than a moveable label. The identity is command-scoped
          # because a CI runner has no git identity and this must never touch
          # user or global configuration.
          git -c user.name="github-actions[bot]" \
              -c user.email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" \
              tag -a "${tag}" -m "${tag}, published to the npm registry by the release workflow" "${SHA}"
          git push origin "refs/tags/${tag}"
dangerousStates.replace:
# ANNOTATED, never lightweight: an annotated tag carries its own
          # object with an author and a date, which is what makes it a record
          # rather than a moveable label. The identity is command-scoped
          # because a CI runner has no git identity and this must never touch
          # user or global configuration.
          git -c user.name="github-actions[bot]" \
              -c user.email="41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com" \
              tag -a "${tag}" -m "${tag}, published to the npm registry by the release workflow" "${SHA}"
          git push --force origin "refs/tags/${tag}"
